correctness.rationale: The repaired result keeps the exact finite linear-word theorem. The absence indicator is the product of four correct pairwise inclusion–exclusion factors. For each forbidden triple set the two-bit suffix transfer counts every word, including arbitrary overlapping factors, and lengths zero and one are handled separately. I checked the infinite rational identity by a separate, unsigned exact computation: after starting with the four two-bit suffixes, use states (observed triple mask, suffix), append a letter unless the complementary triple has been seen, and solve H_state=1+z times the sum of continuation series over legal successors. There are 46 reachable states over 35 masks. The mask never loses a bit, so solving each same-mask block in descending size gives exact rational functions and precisely the displayed numerator and denominator, not just initial terms. Formal division gives 4+2b_n for n>=5. The cubic has one real root and a conjugate pair whose reciprocal growth moduli are lambda^(-1/2) by Vieta; the simple positive pole gives the stated C (checked numerically), and the pole at z=1 contributes four. For lengths one and two the direct run counts are correct; inclusion by length-three prefixes and submultiplicativity justify the threshold and the existence of the rate for larger factor lengths. These checks are unchanged by the repaired attribution and narrower claim of contribution.
residual_risks: The exact enumeration is for finite linear binary words and factor length three only; the asymptotics for higher lengths are not computed here. No formal proof-assistant verification was performed.

evidence: Theorem 17 gives distinct uniform images of ternary squarefree words with complementary factors only 0,1,01,10. Since the ternary squarefree family is exponential, the qualitative threshold at three follows with the elementary small-length bounds; uniform block lengths and truncation give the same positivity over all lengths.
The indexed exact restricted results cover cube-free length-six avoidance at an extremum, complementary-factor spectra of four-run words, and the marked cyclic length-four model, respectively.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The construction proves a positive-growth subfamily and the indexed results cover other scopes, but none provides a count of every finite linear word at every length for complementary triples. The threshold is credited, not carried as a novel claim.

evidence: Avoidance at length three is equivalent to avoidance of all complementary pairs at lengths at least three, by taking prefixes of a hypothetical longer pair. Currie et al. use the equivalent condition in an infinite-word and repetition-restricted setting.

A contiguous antisquare x followed by its complement is not the predicate here. For instance, 0110 passes triple-complement avoidance but is itself a length-four antisquare and is not good in Baranwal et al.'s sense.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The fixed-length versus at-least formulation is an exact alias; neither infinite existence under extra restrictions nor disallowing antisquare concatenations gives the same finite-word language or its exact count.

value.rationale: Complementary-triple avoidance is the smallest nontrivial exponential member of an independently studied avoidance family. The repaired claim computes its entire finite-word enumeration, not just an existence witness or an already familiar base. The recurrence, exact amplitude, and four-word additive correction quantify finite-length and asymptotic behavior that is not determined by the earlier restricted-language or qualitative results. This is a useful natural counting invariant even without a general formula for larger windows.
residual_risks: Value is the precise enumerator for this linear model; it does not rest on claiming the known positivity construction or shared numerical base as new.
